title: Coextension along an isomorphism is restriction along the inverse
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence], there is a natural
isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}
$$
where $\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$ is the coextension functor of
[def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. This is an isomorphism of functors $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$, $\mathcal B=\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$, $F=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, and $H=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence], $F$ is an equivalence with this specified quasi-inverse $H$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] to these two functors and their quasi-inverse isomorphisms to obtain an adjunction $b:F\dashv H$. Write $\varepsilon^H:FH\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ for its counit. The lemma allows adjustment of the equivalence unit to satisfy the triangle identities; we do not assume that arbitrary quasi-inverse isomorphisms already satisfy them.

source.place: clause 5 (invertible morphism), coextension comparison; categorical details in the cited nodes

proof.text: Let $G=\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. The standing hypotheses include that $\mathcal C$ is closed with equalizers, and $\varphi$ is a morphism of monoid objects. Hence [def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction] supplies an adjunction $a:F\dashv G$ whose counit $\varepsilon^G:FG\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ is evaluation at the unit of $\mathcal S$. Thus $G$ and $H$ are right adjoints of the very same functor $F$, with the same source and target categories.

source.place: clause 5 (invertible morphism), coextension comparison; categorical details in the cited nodes

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] with the functor $F$ and the adjunctions $a$ and $b$. Explicitly, for $N\in\mathcal B$ define $\gamma_N:GN\to HN$ as the $b$-transpose of $\varepsilon^G_N:FGN\to N$, and define $\delta_N:HN\to GN$ as the $a$-transpose of $\varepsilon^H_N:FHN\to N$. The cited statement gives naturality of these families and $\delta_N\circ\gamma_N=\mathrm{id}_{GN}$, $\gamma_N\circ\delta_N=\mathrm{id}_{HN}$. Therefore the family $\gamma_N$ defines the required natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$. Its orientation is fixed by $\varepsilon^H_N\circ F(\gamma_N)=\varepsilon^G_N$.
